# Symptom-to-Mechanism Diagnostic Matrix: Java 21 Virtual Threads

This triage ledger maps observed production symptoms directly to root JVM mechanisms, HotSpot invariants, and surgical remediation actions.

---

## Triage Matrix

| ID | Observed Symptom Description | Root HotSpot / JVM Mechanism | Invariant / Diagnostic Signature | Definitive Remediation Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SYM-01** | **JVM-Wide Throughput Collapse across Unrelated Endpoints**<br>A slow/blocking request on one endpoint freezes completely independent, fast endpoints. | **Intrinsic Monitor Pinning (`synchronized`)**<br>Virtual thread holds an `ObjectMonitor` while blocking (I/O, sleep). Continuation cannot unmount. Carrier pool exhausted (especially under 1-CPU container quotas). | JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events emitted (if $> 20\text{ms}$). Carrier pool active worker count equals `parallelism`. | Refactor `synchronized` critical sections to `java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock`. |
| **SYM-02** | **Multi-Second Carrier Stalls with Zero JFR Pinning Events**<br>Carriers completely freeze for seconds; throughput drops to zero; JFR recording shows 0 `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events. | **Silent Native Carrier Capture (`_thread_in_native`)**<br>Native JNI downcalls (SQLite C API, native sleep), Panama FFM, or POSIX `getaddrinfo` run native machine instructions. `VirtualThread.park()` is never called, so `postPinnedEvent` is bypassed. | Exactly 0 JFR pinning events. OS thread profiling / `pstack` shows carrier thread executing native code or kernel wait. | Offload native blocking calls to dedicated bounded platform thread pools (`Executors.newFixedThreadPool`); configure JVM DNS caching (`networkaddress.cache.ttl`). |
| **SYM-03** | **High-Frequency Microservice Latency Spikes Masked in Profiling**<br>p99 latency degrades significantly under concurrency, yet standard production JFR profiling reports 0 pinning events. | **JFR 20 ms Event Suppression**<br>Default JFR profiles (`default.jfc`, `profile.jfc`) configure `<setting name="threshold">20 ms</setting>`. Carrier pins lasting between 1 ms and 19.9 ms are silently suppressed. | Discrepancy between p99 latency and JFR events. Pinning appears only when custom JFR profile with `threshold=0ms` is applied. | Audit with custom JFR template specifying `threshold=0ms` or run with JVM argument `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full`. |
| **SYM-04** | **ReentrantLock Eliminates Pinning but Endpoint Throughput Stagnates**<br>Replacing `synchronized` with `ReentrantLock` unmounts carriers and frees other endpoints, but target endpoint throughput remains flat (e.g. 2 req/s). | **Amdahl's Law Critical Section Serialization Ceiling**<br>Mutual exclusion limits maximum throughput to $X_{max} \le 1 / D_{critical}$. A 500 ms critical section mathematically caps throughput to 2.0 req/s regardless of thread unmounting. | 0 JFR pinning events; low CPU utilization; lock queue depth $> 0$ (`lock.getQueueLength()`). | Shrink critical section duration; transition to optimistic CAS (`AtomicReference`), partitioned striped locks, or lock-free monotonic algorithms (Bernstein's conditions). |
| **SYM-05** | **Downstream Connection Pool Exhaustion (`SQLTransientConnectionException`)**<br>Under virtual threads, database queries fail with connection acquisition timeouts while Tomcat worker metrics report 0 queueing. | **Downstream Pool Queue Shifting**<br>Eliminating Tomcat's platform thread barrier (`maxThreads`) allows all incoming requests to enter the service layer concurrently, shifting the queue to HikariCP. | Spikes in HikariCP `PendingConnections`; `SQLTransientConnectionException: Connection is not available, request timed out`. | Enforce backpressure at HikariCP (`maximumPoolSize`); avoid layering Semaphores over pools (Billy Korando Sip #94); configure admission throttling (`SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor.setConcurrencyLimit`). |
| **SYM-06** | **Bimodal Tail Latency and Starvation under Lock Contention**<br>p999 latency balloons by orders of magnitude; older queued requests are starved while new requests complete quickly. | **AQS Direct-CAS Barging (`NonfairSync`)**<br>Default `ReentrantLock(false)` uses `NonfairSync`. Newly arriving virtual threads CAS directly on state `0`, jumping ahead of threads parked in the AQS wait queue. | High latency variance; virtual threads parked in AQS queue while lock acquisitions succeed immediately from newly arriving callers. | Evaluate `new ReentrantLock(true)` (FairSync) where strict FIFO ordering is required, or stripe locks to eliminate contention. |
| **SYM-07** | **In-Flight Requests & Transactions Evaporate on Container Shutdown**<br>During rolling deployments or pod stops, database records are half-written and client connections drop without clean error responses. | **Virtual Thread Daemon Immutability (JEP 444)**<br>Virtual threads are permanently daemon threads; `setDaemon(false)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. When non-daemon threads exit, JVM halts immediately without unwinding virtual threads. | Premature TCP connection reset (`ECONNRESET`) in clients; incomplete database transactions without rollback logs. | Configure Spring Boot graceful shutdown: `server.shutdown=graceful` with bounded `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase=30s`. |
| **SYM-08** | **OutOfMemoryError / Direct Memory Exhaustion / Young-Gen GC Churn**<br>Spikes in heap usage or native direct memory exhaustion occur when virtual thread count scales to tens of thousands. | **ThreadLocal Bloat, Netty Cache Misuse, & StackChunks**<br>Unbounded `ThreadLocal` allocations, Netty `useCacheForAllThreads=true`, or legacy Jackson (`< 2.16`) buffer recyclers multiply per-virtual-thread. Continuation stacks allocate heap `StackChunk`s. | Heap dumps show millions of `StackChunk` or `BufferRecycler` instances; native direct memory exhaustion. | Upgrade to Jackson $\ge 2.16$ (`sharedLockFreePool()`); verify Netty `useCacheForAllThreads=false`; replace ThreadLocals with Scoped Values; size heap `-Xmx`. |
| **SYM-09** | **Cold-Start Latency Stalls on Initial Requests After Startup**<br>First requests to an endpoint experience multi-second freezes and carrier stalls, while subsequent warm requests execute in sub-milliseconds. | **Class Loading & Static Initializer Pinning (`<clinit>`)**<br>JVM class loading acquires internal class loader monitors (`JarUrlClassLoader` / `LaunchedClassLoader` #51463/#50925) and `<clinit>` pins carriers across ALL JDK versions (including JDK 24+ JEP 491). | JFR pinning events during startup pointing to `ClassLoader.loadClass` or `<clinit>`; absent during steady state. | Pre-warm classes and Spring beans before receiving live traffic; unpack executable fat JARs (`jar -xf`) in container images. |
